instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.72(A) requires each legislative agent and employer to file an initial registration statement within ten days following an engagement, and §101.71(A) makes it unlawful to knowingly fail to register.

Section 101.72(F) provides that the registration card and registration are valid from issuance until the next thirty-first day of December of an even-numbered year, making the registration period biennial (up to ~24 months).

Section 101.72(D)(2) requires written notification of termination of an engagement within thirty days; changes to other required information are to be reflected in the next updated (tri-annual) registration statement.
Section 101.72(A) requires each legislative agent and employer to file the initial registration statement within ten days following an engagement of a legislative agent.

Section 101.72(A) requires each legislative agent AND employer to file an initial registration statement, and §101.72(C) requires a separate initial and updated registration statement for each engagement, indicating separate filings by lobbyist and employer.
Section 101.72(A) enumerates the required contents of the initial registration statement (name, business address, occupation, employer, description of legislation) and does not require a photograph.

Section 101.70(E) excludes from "actively advocate" persons who instruct or petition public officers, and §101.72(E) addresses officers/employees of state agencies who actively advocate in a fiduciary capacity as representatives of the agency, exempting them from expenditure statement filing requirements (though the agency pays the registration fee).

Section 101.72(E) provides that an officer or employee of a state agency who actively advocates in a fiduciary capacity as a representative of that state agency need not file expenditure statements under §101.73, partially relieving government from regulations imposed on non-government lobbyists.
